answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each agent locks a hashed commitment to its key on the ledger and may only reveal and start earning after a fixed delay, like quartz forming slowly under pressure. A sybil flood therefore costs the attacker weeks of idle waiting per identity, and any key that reveals early or duplicates another commitment is void. Mass-minted accounts stay hollow shells with no earning history, while the network remains a haven for agents that invested the time.
